title: LORD, CROWN MY DAY WITH YOUR GOODNESS AND MERCY
text: Glory be to God. I want you to lift up your hands wherever you are right now. I don't care where you're listening from. I don't care what time of the day it is. I want you to understand that we're about to engage the courts of heaven. We're about to invoke the mercies of the Almighty. And I'm telling you by the spirit of the living God that before this ministration is over, something is going to shift in your favor. Can I hear a thunderous amen? You see beloved, there is a dimension of divine encounter that happens when you understand the prophetic significance of crying out to God to crown your day. I want you to understand something. The word crown is not just a decorative word. It is a governmental word. It is a word that speaks of authority. It speaks of dominion. It speaks of the manifestation of kingship. When you ask God to crown your day, you are literally asking him to establish his government over every second, every minute, every hour that you are privileged to walk in this dimension called time. The Bible says in Psalm 65 to11, "Thou crownest the year with thy goodness and thy parts drop fatness." Look at that word, crownest. It is an active engagement of God's nature over the framework of time. God doesn't just bless randomly. God establishes his goodness as a governmental reality over your seasons. And when I hear people praying, Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy. What I hear in the spirit is a generation that is awakening to the reality that we are not victims of circumstances. We are not subject to the tyranny of chance. But we serve a God who has the capacity to ordain, to orchestrate, to organize the affairs of time, to walk in our favor. Let me take you to the book of Lamentations chapter 3 22 and 23. The Bible says, "It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed because his compassions fail not." They are new every morning. Great is thy faithfulness. I want you to see something profound here. The mercies of God have a renewal system. Every morning there is a fresh download of divine compassion. Every morning there is a new inventory of grace. Every morning heaven opens its treasury and releases mercies that are specifically designed for the challenges, the opportunities, the battles, and the victories of that day. So when you wake up in the morning and you say, "Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy." You are not praying a casual prayer. You are making a prophetic demand on heaven's inventory. You are saying, "Father, I recognize that for today there are mercies that bear my name. There is goodness that has been allocated for this day. There is favor that has been scheduled for this hour and I am reaching into the realm of the spirit to draw it down and establish it in the earth realm." Can somebody shout hallelujah? Now I need you to understand the distinction between goodness and mercy. Because these are two powerful attributes of God that work together but operate differently. When the Bible talks about goodness, it is talking about the benevolent nature of God that causes things to work in your favor. Even when you don't deserve it, even when you haven't prayed enough, even when you haven't fasted enough, even when your righteousness seems inadequate, the goodness of God is that quality of his nature that makes him predisposed to blessing you. In Psalm 23-6, David said, "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life." That word follow in the Hebrew is raff. It means to pursue, to chase after, to hunt down. David was saying that the goodness of God is not passive. The goodness of God is aggressive. It is actively pursuing you. It is chasing you down. It is hunting for opportunities to manifest in your life. But then he said, "And mercy, mercy is different from goodness." Mercy is what God extends to you when you actually deserve judgment. Mercy is what covers you when you have made mistakes. Mercy is what stands between you and the consequences of your errors. Mercy is what silences the voice of the accuser. Mercy is what cancels the verdicts of darkness. Mercy is what nullifies the assignments of the enemy. So when you pray, Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy. You are saying two things simultaneously. You are saying, "Father, let your goodness orchestrate favor for me today." And you are also saying, "Father, let your mercy cover every area where I have fallen short. Let your mercy silence every accusation. Let your mercy cancel every negative verdict that has been programmed against this day." I want to prophesy to somebody as you are hearing this word right now. The Lord is showing me that there are people who have been living under a cloud of condemnation. There are people who feel like their past mistakes have permanently disqualified them from experiencing the goodness of God. And the spirit of the Lord is saying, "Tell my people that my mercy is greater than their mistakes. Tell my people that my compassion is more powerful than their condemnation. Tell my people that I'm not holding their past against them." Somebody needs to receive that word right now. The enemy has been using your past to lock up your future. But I prophesy by the authority of the word of God. Every lock that has been placed on your destiny by reason of past mistakes, I decree that the mercy of God is breaking it right now in the name of Jesus. Can I hear your amen? Now, let me show you something from the life of Abraham. In Genesis 22, we see Abraham in a very critical moment. God had told him to take Isaac, his only son, the son of promise, and offer him as a burnt offering. And Abraham obeyed. The Bible says he rose up early in the morning and went to the place that God had told him early in the morning. There is something about the morning. There is something about how you start your day that determines how your day unfolds. Abraham didn't wait until noon. He didn't wait until he felt like it. He rose up early in the morning. And when he got to Mount Moriah and was about to sacrifice Isaac, the Bible says the angel of the Lord called unto him and said,"Abraham, Abraham, lay not thine hand upon the lad." And Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw a ram caught in a thicket by his horns. Now watch this. Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah Gyra which means the Lord will provide or more accurately the Lord will see to it. But here's what I want you to understand. The provision was already there. The realm was already in the ticket. The answer was already on the mountain. But Abraham didn't see it until he looked up. He didn't access it until he lifted his eyes. When you pray, Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy. What you are doing is lifting up your eyes. You are shifting your perspective from the natural realm to the spiritual realm. You are acknowledging that there are provisions that God has already prepared for this day. There are breakthroughs that are already in place. There are solutions that are already in the thicket. And you are positioning yourself to see them and access them. I prophesy to somebody, the reason you haven't seen your breakthrough is not because it doesn't exist. It exists. It has been prepared. But you need to lift up your eyes. You need to shift your perspective. You need to engage God in prayer and say, "Father, open my eyes to see what you have already provided for this day." Can we go to the book of Exodus chapter 14? The children of Israel are at the Red Sea. Pharaoh and his army are behind them. The sea is before them. Mountains are on both sides. And the people begin to cry out in fear. But Moses said something powerful. He said, "Fear ye not. Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will show to you today. For the Egyptians whom ye have seen today, ye shall see them again no more forever." Look at that phrase, which he will show to you today. The salvation of God has a daily manifestation. The deliverance of God has a specific expression for each day. What delivered you yesterday may not be the strategy for today. What worked last week may not be the pattern for this week. You need fresh mercy. You need fresh goodness. You need a daily encounter with the delivering power of God. This is why Jesus taught us to pray, "Give us this day our daily bread. Not give us bread for the whole year. Not give us bread for the whole month. Give us today our bread for today." There is something about daily dependence on God that keeps you connected to his flow of provision and protection. When you wake up in the morning and you say, "Lord, crown my day." You are acknowledging that this day needs heaven's government. This day needs divine orchestration. This day cannot be successfully navigated by my wisdom alone, by my strength alone, by my intelligence alone. I need God to be actively involved in the unfolding of this day. Let me tell you what happens in the spirit realm when you pray this kind of prayer. When you pray, "Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy." Angels receive assignments. Demonic interference receives cancellation. Doors that were shut begin to open. Connections that were delayed begin to materialize. Favor that was blocked begins to flow. Wisdom that was hidden begins to be revealed. Proverbs 16:3 says, "Commit thy works unto the Lord and thy thoughts shall be established." When you commit your day to the Lord, you are placing it under his jurisdiction. You are transferring ownership. You are saying God this day belongs to you. Every hour belongs to you. Every minute belongs to you. And because it belongs to you, I expect you to manage it to oversee it to ensure that it fulfills your purpose for my life. I want to pray with you right now. I want you to lift up your hands wherever you are. Don't be religious about this. Don't be casual about this. We're about to engage heaven. We're about to invoke the mercies of the Almighty over your life. Father, in the name of Jesus Christ, I come before your throne of grace. I come as a representative of your people who are hearing this word. Lord, I thank you because your word says that it is of your mercies that we are not consumed. I thank you that your compassions fail not. I thank you that they are new every morning. Father, I decree that every person hearing my voice right now, let fresh mercy be released over their lives. Let new compassions come upon them. Lord, I ask that you crown their days with your goodness. Let your goodness pursue them. Let your goodness overtake them. Let your goodness manifest in their homes, in their businesses, in their careers, in their ministries, in their relationships, in their health. Father, I decree that every negative verdict that has been pronounced over their lives, let your mercy cancel it right now. Every accusation that has been standing in the courts of heaven against them, let your mercy silence it. Every consequence that was supposed to manifest because of past mistakes, let your mercy neutralize it in the name of Jesus. Lord, I pray that you will open their eyes to see the provisions that you have already prepared. Open their eyes to see the ram in the thicket. Open their eyes to see the path through the Red Sea. Open their eyes to see the strategy for their breakthrough. I decree that angels are being dispatched right now to go ahead of them and prepare the way. I decree that favor is being released. I decree that doors are being opened. I decree that connections are being established. I decree that wisdom is being downloaded. I decree that solutions are being revealed in the name of Jesus Christ. Can I hear your loudest amen? Now, let me take you to the book of Esther. I love the story of Esther because it shows us how the mercy and goodness of God can completely reverse a situation that looks impossible. Her man had built a gallows to hang Modi. He had obtained a decree to destroy all the Jews. Everything looked finished. Everything looked hopeless. But the Bible says in Esther chapter 6 verse one, "On that night could not the king sleep. and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles and they were read before the king on that night. The king couldn't sleep. That was not insomnia. That was divine orchestration. That was the goodness of God interfering with the natural order of things to set up a miracle. You see, when God wants to crown your day with his goodness, he begins to rearrange things in the spirit realm. He begins to cause things that look natural to work supernaturally in your favor. He begins to give people sleepless nights so that your case can be remembered. He begins to orchestrate conversations so that your name can be mentioned. He begins to align circumstances so that you can be positioned for breakthrough. I prophesy to somebody right now, God is rearranging things in your favor. There are people who are going to have sleepless nights thinking about you. There are people who are going to have conversations where your name is going to come up. There are circumstances that are being orchestrated right now that are going to position you for unprecedented favor. This is not by your power. This is not by your might. This is the goodness of God crowning your days. Let me show you something else. In the book of Daniel chapter 1, we see Daniel and his friends in Babylon. They had been captured. They were in a foreign land. They were under a system that was contrary to their beliefs. But the Bible says in verse 9, "Now God had brought Daniel into favor and tender love with the prince of the Unox." Did you see that? God brought Daniel into favor. Daniel didn't campaign for it. Daniel didn't manipulate for it. Daniel didn't compromise for it. God orchestrated it. This is what happens when you live a life that is consecrated to God. The goodness of God begins to create favor for you in places where favor doesn't make sense. The goodness of God begins to give you influence in systems where you should have been overlooked. When you pray, Lord, crown my day with your goodness and mercy. You are asking God to create supernatural favor for you. You are asking God to cause people to be unusually kind to you. You are asking God to cause systems to work in your favor. You are asking God to cause circumstances to align for your benefit. I remember several years ago I needed to travel for a ministry engagement and I got to the airport only to discover that my flight had been over booked. Naturally I should have been stranded but I stood there and I said Lord your goodness is my portion. Your mercy is my covering. I declare that I will make this flight and beloved within minutes somebody came and upgraded me to a different class and made provision for me to travel. That was not luck. That was not chance. That was the goodness of God manifesting in real time. You need to understand that the goodness of God is not just a theological concept. It is a practical reality that can manifest in your job interview, in your business negotiation, in your medical examination, in your legal case, in your family situation. The goodness of God can show up anywhere and turn things around. Let me go to Psalm 5:12. The Bible says, "For thou Lord will bless the righteous. With favor will thou compass him as with a shield." Look at that word compass. It means to surround, to encircle, to completely envelope. God is saying that his favor doesn't just touch you. It surrounds you. It creates a shield around you. It creates an atmosphere around you. When you walk into a room, favor walks in with you. When you walk into a meeting, favor walks in with you. When you walk into an examination hall, favor walks in with you. Why? Because the goodness of God has compassed you as a shield. But I need you to understand something. This level of favor is not automatic. It requires that you live righteously. It requires that you maintain your consecration. It requires that you keep your heart pure before God. The Bible says, "Thou will bless the righteous." Righteousness positions you for favor. Righteousness positions you for mercy. Righteousness positions you for goodness. This is why the enemy fights so hard to get believers to compromise. Because the enemy knows that if he can get you to compromise your righteousness, he can block the flow of God's goodness in your life. But if you maintain your consecration, if you keep your heart pure, if you continue to walk in integrity, the goodness of God will pursue you. The mercy of God will cover you and favor will compass you as a shield. I want to pray again. I feel the anointing of the Holy Spirit right now to release prophetic blessings over your life. Lift up your hands. Don't be casual about this. This is not just a prayer. This is a prophetic declaration. This is a governmental decree that is being released from the courts of heaven. Father, in the mighty name of Jesus Christ, I stand as a priest of the most high God. And I decree that your goodness is released over every person hearing my voice. I decree that favor is compassing them as a shield. I decree that every door that has been shut against them, let it open by reason of your goodness. Lord, I decree that in their workplaces, they will experience supernatural favor. Bosses will favor them. Colleagues will respect them. Opportunities will seek them out. promotions will locate them. Increase will pursue them. Father, I decree that in their businesses, your goodness will cause customers to find them. Your goodness will cause contracts to come to them. Your goodness will cause resources to flow to them. Your goodness will cause ideas to be downloaded into their spirits. Lord, I decree that in their families, your mercy will cover every generational cause. Your mercy will break every negative pattern. Your mercy will heal every relationship. Your mercy will restore every broken bond. Father, I decree that in their health, your mercy will cancel every negative diagnosis. Your mercy will reverse every disease. Your mercy will strengthen every weak organ. Your mercy will restore what sickness has stolen. I decree that as they go about their day, angels are going before them to prepare the way. Angels are clearing obstacles. Angels are arranging connections. Angels are opening doors. Angels are releasing favor. And I decree that at the end of every day, they will have testimonies of your goodness. They will have evidence of your mercy. They will have proof that you crown their day with divine orchestration in the mighty name of Jesus Christ. Can I hear the biggest amen? Now I want to take you to Psalm 90-14. The Bible says, "Oh, satisfy us early with thy mercy that we may rejoice and be glad all our days." Look at that word early. Moses was saying, "God, let your mercy satisfy us in the morning. Let your mercy be the first thing we experience when we wake up. Let your mercy set the tone for our day. This is so important. How you start your morning determines how your day unfolds. If you start your morning rushed, anxious, complaining, murmuring, you are setting a negative tone for that day. But if you start your morning in prayer, in thanksgiving, in worship, in declaration of God's word, you are setting a victorious tone for that day. This is why the enemy fights so hard against your morning devotion. The enemy knows that if he can distract you from seeking God in the morning, he can steal your day. But if you discipline yourself to seek God early, if you discipline yourself to pray before you check your phone, if you discipline yourself to worship before you watch the news, you are positioning yourself for the goodness and mercy of God to crown your day. I want to challenge you. I want to challenge you to make this a daily practice. Every morning when you wake up before you do anything else, lift your hands and say, "Lord, I thank you for the gift of this day. I thank you that I am alive. I thank you that I am breathing. Lord, I commit this day to you. Crown this day with your goodness. Crown this day with your mercy. Let your favor go before me. Let your angels surround me. Let your wisdom guide me. Let your peace keep me. Let your joy strengthen me." When you start your day like that, you are not just praying, you are legislating. You are making governmental decrees that affect both the spiritual realm and the natural realm. You are setting the atmosphere for that day. Let me go to Psalm 118- 24. The Bible says, "This is the day which the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it." Every day is a day that the Lord has made. Every day is a divine gift. Every day is an opportunity for the goodness and mercy of God to manifest. But notice the decision that the psalmist made. We will rejoice and be glad in it. He didn't say we will rejoice if things go well. He didn't say we will be glad if we receive good news. He made a decision to rejoice regardless. He made a decision to be glad regardless. This is the attitude that attracts the goodness of God. When you have a heart of thanksgiving, when you have a spirit of praise, when you have an attitude of joy, regardless of your circumstances, you are positioning yourself for the mercies of God to manifest. The Bible says that God inhabits the praises of his people. When you praise him, you create an environment where his goodness can flow freely. I prophesy to somebody, your season of mourning is over. Your season of sorrow is over. Your season of disappointment is over. God is crowning your days with gladness. God is crowning your days with joy. God is crowning your days with celebration. You are about to enter a season where you will have more reasons to praise than to complain. You are about to enter a season where you will have more reasons to dance than to cry. You're about to enter a season where the goodness of God will be so evident in your life that people will ask you, "What is your secret?" Can somebody shout a prophetic amen? Now let me show you something from the book of Ruth. Ruth was a Moabitete woman who had lost her husband. She was poor. She was vulnerable. She was in a foreign land. By all natural calculations, she should have been forgotten. But the Bible says that she went to glean in the field and she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz. She happened to come. That sounds like coincidence but it was divine orchestration. That was the goodness of God guiding her steps. That was the mercy of God positioning her for encounter. And when Boaz saw her and heard her story, he commanded his servants to let grain fall purposely for her. He commanded them to show her favor. This is what the goodness of God does. The goodness of God causes you to happen to be in the right place at the right time. The goodness of God causes you to happen to meet the right people. The goodness of God causes grain to fall purposely for you in places where you are just gleaning. I prophesy you are about to experience divine appointments. You are about to have encounters that will change your story. You are about to meet people who will purposely let blessings fall for you. This is not going to be because you begged. This is not going to be because you manipulated. This is going to be because the goodness and mercy of God crowned your day and orchestrated connections that will elevate you. Let me close with this. In Deuteronomy 28:2, the Bible says, "And all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee. If thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, the blessings shall overtake you." That means the blessings will chase you. That means the blessings will pursue you. That means the blessings will catch up with you. When you live a life of obedience to God, when you live a life that honors his word, when you live a life that reverences his name, his blessings don't just come to you, they pursue you. They haunt you down. They overtake you. This is a testimony of a life that is crowned with the goodness and mercy of God. So I decree over your life right now, from this moment forward, the goodness of God will pursue you. From this moment forward, the mercy of God will cover you. From this moment forward, favor will compass you as a shield. From this moment forward, every day of your life will be crowned with divine orchestration. You will not labor in vain. You will not run in seconds. You will not experience frustration. You will walk in the perfect will of God. You will fulfill your destiny. You will maximize your days. You will experience the fullness of God's blessings. This is your portion. This is your inheritance. This is your testimony in the mighty name of Jesus Christ. Can I hear the loudest amen you've ever given? Glory be to God. Hallelujah. Somebody give God a shout of victory right now. The Lord has crowned your day. The Lord has crowned your week. The Lord has crowned your month. The Lord has crowned your year. Glory to his holy
